_README: Recorded 2026-09-09 during W1-D7-08, from three real ExtendFootprintTTLOp transactions on
public Stellar Testnet against guinea-pig A. Source account evergreen-b, which holds no
authority over A and needs none.
This is the empirical anchor W2-D9-02 validates the rent model against. It exists because the
extends had to happen anyway - A was nine days from archival - so the validation data was a
by-product rather than something to manufacture.
rentFeeCharged is isolated from resultMetaXdr's SorobanTransactionMetaExtV1, NOT inferred from
fee_charged. fee_charged bundles the base fee and the non-refundable resource fee with rent;
quoting it as 'the rent' overstates rent by 1.5-4.4% here and by more on entries with real
Sizes are byte lengths of the base64-decoded XDR from the pre-extend getLedgerEntries response
Ledger numbers are historical and testnet resets. The FEE RELATIONSHIPS are the durable part.

observations.claim: Durability class is a first-order price term, independent of size.
observations.basis: The persistent and temporary entries are byte-for-byte the same size (88B data, 76B key) and were extended by 1,312,937 and 1,312,939 ledgers - a two-ledger difference. Persistent rent was 1.952x temporary.
observations.confidence: high - the only variable that differs is durability

observations.claim: Rent is 95.6-98.5% of the fee; the non-refundable component is roughly flat.
observations.basis: nonRefundableResourceFeeCharged was 2,237-2,359 stroops across all three, while rent ranged 53,196-154,503. A model that estimates only rent is within ~4.4% here.
observations.confidence: high for extend-only transactions - a bump with a real read/write footprint will not behave this way

observations.claim: A wrong mechanism that predicts the right number is worse than no mechanism.
observations.basis: These fees were first reported as 'the instance cost 2.8x the temporary entry, because rent is priced per entry size'. The 2.8x is real - 156,840 / 55,655 - and the sentence survives casual checking because its number is right. The mechanism is not: the persistent and temporary entries are byte-identical and still differ by 1.95x, so durability was doing the work attributed to size. Isolating rentFeeCharged is what exposed it; fee_charged alone would have left the wrong explanation standing.
observations.confidence: recorded as process, not as a measurement - it is why this fixture asserts relationships instead of a formula

observations.claim: Rent grows with size, but three points do not determine how.
observations.basis: instance vs persistent is 1.545x the entry data (136B vs 88B) but 1.488x the rent, and 1.122x the key+data total. Neither total bytes nor data bytes predicts it exactly. Do NOT fit a coefficient to this.
observations.confidence: low - stated so W2-D9-02 knows this is the gap, not an answer

observations.claim: The 1.952x durability ratio is exactly 2:1 in the protocol, and the constant that produces it was published all along.
observations.basis: Read 2026-09-10 from the live STATE_ARCHIVAL config entry: persistent_rent_rate_denominator = 1215, temp_rent_rate_denominator = 2430. Exactly 2:1. The measured 1.952x is that ratio with the flat non-refundable components folded in, so the residual is accounted for rather than being noise in a three-point measurement.
observations.confidence: high - this is protocol configuration read from the chain, not an inference from these three transactions
observations.note: Pleasing shape worth keeping: this fixture explicitly forbade fitting a coefficient to three points, and the coefficient turned out to be published in the network config. The instinct to refuse the fit was right, and the reward for refusing it was the real number rather than a fitted one. The size coefficient (see size-scaling-unresolved) remains unresolved and is NOT in this config - do not read this entry as licence to fit that one.
